Both are inverse associations between irisin and FPG. Same exposure (serum/circulating irisin), same outcome (FPG), same direction. Populations differ (T2DM adults vs healthy schoolchildren boys), but contextual comparison is allowed. Both cross-sectional. Concordant.

Decision: concordant, factor none.

source_evidence.quote: the level of irisin decreased as the levels of FPG and fasting insulin (FINS) increased
After adjusting for age, the irisin level in boys was negatively related to fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (r = -0.21, P = .006).

verdict.label: concordant
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an inverse association between circulating irisin and fasting plasma glucose. Source A (PMID 40241486) states that in T2DM patients 'the level of irisin decreased as the levels of FPG and fasting insulin (FINS) increased' (sentence 4). Source B (PMID 33592858) reports that in boys, after adjusting for age, 'the irisin level in boys was negatively related to fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (r = -0.21, P = .006)' (sentence 7). The exposure (irisin), outcome (FPG), contrast type (association), and direction (negative/inverse) match. The populations differ (adults with T2DM vs. generally healthy Taiwanese schoolchildren, boys subgroup), but this permits contextual comparison rather than exclusion; both are cross-sectional association analyses. Both report the same directional finding, so the pair is concordant.
